title: SSC GD 2024 Musical Instrument & Musicians PART-2

questions.question: The Sangeet Natak Akademi is India's national academy for music, dance and drama. It was created by a resolution of the (then) _________, Government of India, in 1952 with Dr P.V. Rajamannar as its first Chairman.
questions.solution:
The Sangeet Natak Akademi, established in 1952, was created by a resolution of the Ministry of Education.
  • Dr. P.V. Rajamannar served as its first Chairman, inaugurated by Dr. Rajendra Prasad.
  • The academy serves as the apex body for performing arts in India to preserve and promote music, dance, and drama.
  • Note: It is currently an autonomous body under the Ministry of Culture, but its inception was under the education portfolio.

questions.question: Who of the following is famous for playing musical instrument Kanjira?
questions.solution:
Pudukkotai Dakshinamurthi Pillai was a legendary percussionist renowned for his mastery of the Kanjira and the Mridangam.
  • The Kanjira is a South Indian frame drum belonging to the tambourine family, traditionally made with monitor lizard skin.
  • Pannalal Ghosh is associated with the Flute, while Kishan Maharaj is a Tabla maestro.

questions.question:
Match the following personalities with their associated musical instrument:

A) S. Balachander

B) Anushka Shankar

C) Kishan Maharaj

1 Tabla

2 Veena

3 Sitar
questions.solution:
This matching identifies masters of distinct Indian instruments:
  • S. Balachander: A celebrated virtuoso of the Veena, an ancient plucked string instrument.
  • Anushka Shankar: A world-renowned Sitar player and daughter of Pandit Ravi Shankar.
  • Kishan Maharaj: A legendary exponent of the Tabla belonging to the Benaras Gharana.

questions.question: On which Indian musician's life was the documentary film “Bansuri Guru” based on?
questions.solution:
The documentary film “Bansuri Guru” (directed by Rajeev Chaurasia) is based on the life of Hari Prasad Chaurasia.
  • He is globally recognized as a master of the Bansuri (bamboo flute) in the Hindustani classical tradition.
  • Additional Info: He has collaborated with international artists and composed music for several Indian films under the name 'Shiv-Hari' alongside Shivkumar Sharma.

questions.question: Shiv Kumar Sharma's name is synonymous with _________ Indian classical music instrument.
questions.solution:
Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma is the musician who single-handedly elevated the Santoor from a Kashmiri folk instrument to a respected classical status.
  • The Santoor is a trapezoid-shaped hammered dulcimer with 72 strings.
  • He was awarded the Padma Vibhushan in 2001 for his immense contribution to music.

questions.question: Renowned violinist - _________ trained in Carnatic music as well as Western classical music.
questions.solution:
Lakshminarayana Subramaniam (L. Subramaniam) is a prolific violinist and composer trained in both Carnatic and Western classical traditions.
  • He is famous for his 'Global Fusion' projects and orchestral compositions.
  • Note: His technique incorporates traditional Indian slides (gamakas) with Western bowing styles.

questions.question: Who is famous for playing the musical instrument shehnai?
questions.solution:
Ali Ahmad Hussain was a prominent Shehnai player from Kolkata who helped maintain the instrument's popularity alongside Bismillah Khan.
  • The Shehnai is a double-reed oboe-like instrument, traditionally played during weddings and festivals.
  • N. Ramani and Hari Prasad Chaurasia are flute players, while Rajaratanam Pillai was a Nadaswaram master.

questions.question: Pandit Birju Maharaj was an Indian dancer, composer, singer, and exponent of the __________ "Kalka-Bindadin" Gharana of Kathak dance in India.
questions.solution:
Pandit Birju Maharaj was the leading exponent of the Lucknow "Kalka-Bindadin" Gharana of Kathak.
  • He was a descendant of the Maharaj family of Kathak dancers, which includes his uncles Shambhu Maharaj and Lachhu Maharaj.
  • Kathak is a major classical dance form of Northern India characterized by rhythmic footwork and spins.

questions.question: Ustad Binda Khan is associated with which of the following instruments?
questions.solution:
Ustad Binda Khan was one of the greatest masters of the Sarangi in the 20th century.
  • The Sarangi is a bowed, short-necked string instrument known for its ability to mimic the nuances of the human voice.
  • He belonged to the Delhi Gharana and was instrumental in modernizing Sarangi solo performances.

questions.question: Ustad Bismillah Khan is a famous exponent of _________ .
questions.solution:
Ustad Bismillah Khan is the most iconic exponent of the Shehnai.
  • He is credited with bringing the Shehnai to the concert stage, as it was previously restricted to ritualistic ceremonies.
  • Achievement: He was awarded the Bharat Ratna (India's highest civilian award) in 2001.

questions.question: Which instrument is played by Pandit Ravi Shankar?
questions.solution:
Pandit Ravi Shankar was a world-famous virtuoso of the Sitar.
  • He was a major ambassador for Indian music in the West and famously taught George Harrison of The Beatles.
  • He founded the Maihar Gharana style of playing, characterized by deep technical precision and melodic exploration.

questions.question: Which iconic Indian classical vocalist, often known as the "Mewati Maestro," is celebrated for his mastery of khayal singing and his innovative approach to ragas?
questions.solution:
Pandit Jasraj was a legendary vocalist of the Mewati Gharana.
  • He is celebrated for his Khayal singing, a modern genre of classical vocal music focused on imagination and improvisation.
  • He created a unique form of jugalbandi (duet) called 'Jasrangi' based on the Moorchhana technique.

questions.question: Krishna Rao Shankar Pandit, Raja Bhaiya Poonchwale are associated with which Gharana?
questions.solution:
Krishna Rao Shankar Pandit and Raja Bhaiya Poonchwale are pillars of the Gwalior Gharana.
  • The Gwalior Gharana is considered the oldest 'Khyal' Gharana and the foundation from which many others evolved.
  • It is known for its simplicity, clarity of notes, and emphasis on 'Raga' purity.

questions.question: Who of the following singer popularized the Sambalpuri folk song ‘Rangabati Rangabati’?
questions.solution:
Krishna Patel, along with Jitendra Haripal, is the singer who popularized the famous Sambalpuri folk song ‘Rangabati’.
  • This song is a cultural icon of Odisha and was first recorded in the 1970s.
  • Note: The song became a national sensation and has been re-rendered in various modern languages and films.

questions.question: Which iconic playback singer, known for his mesmerizing voice and classic hits like "Mere Sapno Ki Rani Kab Aayegi Tu," was also a music director and composer?
questions.solution:
Kishore Kumar was a multi-talented artist known as a playback singer, actor, and music director.
  • He won a record 8 Filmfare Awards for Best Male Playback Singer.
  • While he never had formal training in classical music, his versatile voice allowed him to master various moods from soulful melodies to yodeling.

questions.question: ________ choreographed famous song ‘Kahe Chhed Mohe’ from the movie Devdas and ‘Mohe Rang Do Laal’ from Bajirao Mastani.
questions.solution:
Pandit Birju Maharaj was not only a dancer but also a prolific choreographer for Indian cinema.
  • He choreographed the Kathak sequences in Sanjay Leela Bhansali's Devdas and Bajirao Mastani.
  • His work in films helped bring the authenticity of classical Kathak to a mainstream audience.

questions.question: Which instrument was played by Ustad Asad Ali Khan?
questions.solution:
Ustad Asad Ali Khan was one of the last great masters of the Rudra Veena, playing in the Khandarbani style.
  • The Rudra Veena is a large plucked string instrument used in Dhrupad music, featuring two large gourds (tumbas).
  • He was honored with the Padma Bhushan in 2008.

questions.question: Who is famous for playing the percussion instrument Tabla?
questions.solution:
Ustad Allah Rakha was a renowned maestro of the Tabla and a frequent accompanist to Pandit Ravi Shankar.
  • He belonged to the Punjab Gharana and is credited with popularizing the Tabla worldwide.
  • Fact: He is the father of the equally famous Tabla player, Zakir Hussain.

questions.question: Which instrument is played by Amjad Ali Khan?
questions.solution:
Ustad Amjad Ali Khan is a world-renowned master of the Sarod.
  • The Sarod is a fretless string instrument known for its deep, introspective sound and ability to produce continuous slides (meend).
  • He represents the sixth generation of the Bangash lineage of musicians.

questions.question: Ustad Zakir Hussain plays ________ .
questions.solution:
Ustad Zakir Hussain is the most famous contemporary player of the Tabla.
  • He is a child prodigy who transitioned from classical accompaniment to international fame through fusion bands like Shakti.
  • He is widely regarded as an international phenomenon in the world of percussion and rhythmic composition.
